HIGH.title: FastModel + use_rslora=True causes gradient explosion at block_size=384 (stable at 1024, workaround: pure HF PEFT)
HIGH.problem: RS-LoRA training explodes at short block size while the equivalent HF/PEFT run stays stable.
HIGH.fix: Isolate the FastModel-specific numerical path and compare gradients/loss against the reference.
HIGH.gate: Controlled same-seed model/GPU experiment required; this is a report, not a confirmed implementation cause.

audit.title: FastModel + use_rslora=True causes gradient explosion at block_size=384 (stable at 1024, workaround: pure HF PEFT)
audit.body:
Environment

- Unsloth 2026.4.8, Transformers 5.5.0, Torch 2.6.0+cu124
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX 3060 12GB, CUDA 8.6
- Model: google/gemma-3-4b-it
- Adapter: RS-LoRA (use_rslora=True), r=32, alpha=32

Description

When using FastModel with use_rslora=True and block_size=384, gradient norms explode catastrophically from step 1 (grad_norms 50–105) regardless of learning rate, including during warmup when LR is near zero. The same configuration at block_size=1024 is stable (grad_norms 7–11). Replacing FastModel with standard HuggingFace AutoModelForCausalLM + PEFT get_peft_model at block_size=384 produces healthy grad_norms (4–6) and converges normally to train_loss ~2.45.
The LR-independence rules out optimizer misconfiguration. The issue appears specific to FastModel — FastLanguageModel (Gemma 3 12B runs) and FastVisionModel (Gemma 4 E2B runs) did not exhibit this behaviour at comparable block sizes.

Reproduction

```
# Catastrophic — FastModel + RS-LoRA + block_size=384
model, tokenizer = FastModel.from_pretrained(
    model_name="google/gemma-3-4b-it",
    max_seq_length=384,
    load_in_4bit=False,
)
model = FastModel.get_peft_model(model, r=32, lora_alpha=32,
    use_rslora=True, use_dora=False, lora_dropout=0,
    target_modules=["q_proj","k_proj","v_proj","o_proj",
                    "gate_proj","up_proj","down_proj"])

# SFTTrainer with block_size=384, lr=5e-5, max_grad_norm=1.0
# → grad_norms 50-105 from step 1

# Stable — FastModel + RS-LoRA + block_size=1024 (same everything else)
# → grad_norms 7-11

# Stable — pure HF PEFT + RS-LoRA + block_size=384
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("google/gemma-3-4b-it",
    dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="auto")
config = LoraConfig(r=32, lora_alpha=32, use_rslora=True,
    target_modules=[...], lora_dropout=0, bias="none",
    task_type=TaskType.CAUSAL_LM)
model = get_peft_model(model, config)
# SFTTrainer with block_size=384, lr=5e-5, max_grad_norm=1.0
# → grad_norms 4-6, train_loss converges to 2.45
```

Hypothesis

The gradient offloading optimisation ("Will smartly offload gradients to save VRAM") may interact with RS-LoRA's alpha/sqrt(r) gradient scaling in a numerically unstable way at shorter sequence lengths. At block_size=384, each optimizer step processes ~3K tokens vs ~8K at 1024. The issue does not appear with FastLanguageModel or FastVisionModel.

Workaround

Use pure HuggingFace PEFT (AutoModelForCausalLM + get_peft_model) when RS-LoRA is required with short block sizes.

nodes.title: fix: use `sys.executable` for pip and python subprocesses to support venv environments
nodes.body:
## Problem

When running from a Python virtual environment (`.venv`, conda, poetry, etc.), GGUF conversion fails because `llama_cpp.py` shells out to bare `pip` and `python` commands, which resolve to the **system** Python — not the interpreter running the current process.

This causes two distinct failures:

### 1. `pip install` hits PEP 668 protection (exit code 1)

`check_pip()` iterates `["uv pip", "pip", "pip3", ...]` and finds the system's `pip`, which on modern Debian/Ubuntu (PEP 668) refuses to install packages outside a virtual environment:

```
RuntimeError: Unsloth: GGUF conversion failed: [FAIL] Command `pip install gguf protobuf sentencepiece mistral_common` failed with exit code 1
stdout: error: externally-managed-environment
```

### 2. `python` command not found during GGUF conversion (exit code 127)

The conversion command is hardcoded as:

```python
command = f"python {converter_location} {args_str} {input_folder}"
```

On many Linux distributions, there is no bare `python` binary — only `python3`. Even where `python` exists, it points to the system Python, not the venv interpreter, so it would lack the required packages.

```
subprocess.CalledProcessError: Command 'python llama.cpp/unsloth_convert_hf_to_gguf.py ...' returned non-zero exit status 127.
```

### 3. `uv pip` fails in non-uv environments (exit code 2)

On systems where `uv` is installed globally but the Python environment is managed by conda, mamba, or a standard venv (not uv), and after https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth-zoo/pull/336 was merged, `check_pip()` finds `uv pip` first (it was the first entry in `PIP_OPTIONS`) and tries to use it. But `uv pip install` requires a uv-managed venv and fails:

```
RuntimeError: [FAIL] Command `uv pip install gguf protobuf sentencepiece mistral_common` failed with exit code 2
stdout: error: No virtual environment found; run `uv venv` to create an environment, or pass `--system` to install into a non-virtual environment
```

By placing `sys.executable -m pip` before `uv pip` in `PIP_OPTIONS`, `check_pip()` now finds a working pip before ever reaching the `uv pip` entry, resolving this issue as well.

## Root Cause

All three issues stem from the same root cause: subprocess calls resolve to system-wide executables instead of the currently-running Python interpreter's environment.

## Fix

Replace bare `pip`/`python` references with `sys.executable`, which always resolves to the Python binary running the current process. This is the [officially recommended way](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/tutorials/installing-packages/#use-pip-for-installing) to invoke pip programmatically.

### Change 1: `PIP_OPTIONS` (line 70)

Prepend `f"{sys.executable} -m pip"` so that `check_pip()` prefers the current interpreter's pip:

```diff
 PIP_OPTIONS = [
+    f"{sys.executable} -m pip",  # Always prefer the running interpreter's pip
     "uv pip",
     "pip",
     "pip3",
     "python3 -m pip",
     "py -m pip",
     "poetry",
 ]
```

### Change 2: GGUF conversion command (line 1030)

Use `sys.executable` instead of bare `python`:

```diff
- command = f"python {converter_location} {args_str} {input_folder}"
+ command = f"{sys.executable} {converter_location} {args_str} {input_folder}"
```

## Why `sys.executable`?

`sys.executable` returns the absolute path of the Python interpreter running the current process. It correctly resolves in **all** common environments:

| Environment | `sys.executable` resolves to | Works? |
|---|---|---|
| Standard venv | `/path/to/.venv/bin/python` | ✅ |
| Conda / Mamba | `/path/to/conda/envs/myenv/bin/python` | ✅ |
| uv | `/path/to/.venv/bin/python` | ✅ |
| Poetry | `/path/to/.venv/bin/python` | ✅ |
| System Python (Colab/Kaggle) | `/usr/bin/python3` | ✅ |

For `check_pip()` specifically, the fallback list still contains `"uv pip"`, `"pip"`, etc., so environments where `sys.executable -m pip` doesn't work (e.g., uv environments that don't ship pip) gracefully fall through to the next option.

## Alternatives Considered

| Approach | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `sys.executable -m pip` / `sys.executable` | ✅ **Chosen.** Standard practice, minimal change, works everywhere |
| Modify `PATH`/`VIRTUAL_ENV` env vars before subprocess calls | ❌ Fragile, assumes venv layout, requires threading `env` through many functions |
| `UNSLOTH_STUDIO=1` env var to switch behavior | ❌ Adds coupling, doesn't fix root cause, easy to forget |
| `--break-system-packages` flag | ❌ Explicitly discouraged by PEP 668, can corrupt system Python |

## Testing

- Verified GGUF export completes successfully from a `.venv` environment on a PEP 668 system (Ubuntu with Python 3.12)
- pip packages install into the correct venv
- `convert_hf_to_gguf.py` runs under the venv Python with access to all required packages
- No behavioral change for non-venv environments (Colab, Kaggle, bare system Python)

audit.title: Unquoted `writeup_file` in `os.popen("chktex ...")` runs shell metacharacters from `idea['Name']`
audit.body:
## What

`ai_scientist/perform_writeup.py:80` (commit `1de1dbc1`) runs `os.popen(f"chktex {writeup_file} -q -n2 -n24 -n13 -n1").read()`. `writeup_file` is built from the raw `idea['Name']` — `launch_scientist.py:167` reads it into `idea_name`, `:168` into `folder_name`, then `perform_writeup.py:16-18` sets `writeup_file = osp.join(cwd, "template.tex")` — with no quoting and no slug check. Shell metacharacters in the idea name execute inside `/bin/sh` before `chktex` is even resolved.

The same sink exists in two places in the separate repo `SakanaAI/AI-Scientist-v2` (HEAD `96bd5161`), which loads ideas via `--load_ideas` (`launch_scientist_bfts.py:52`) rather than `--skip-idea-generation`: `ai_scientist/perform_writeup.py:684` and `ai_scientist/perform_icbinb_writeup.py:1047` (the latter carries a `# TODO: should prob use subprocess instead` comment).

## How to reproduce

The launcher preflight (`launch_scientist.py:109-113`) requires `chktex` and `pdflatex` on `PATH`, so a real run always has `chktex` installed. That does not help: `/bin/sh` evaluates the unquoted `{writeup_file}` before `chktex` runs, so the injection fires with or without `chktex` present — the run below has no `chktex` on `PATH` and still writes the canary.

A poisoned `ideas.json` entry reaches this path under `--skip-idea-generation`, which loads `ideas.json` raw (`generate_ideas.py:84-92`); the entry needs `"novel": true` to pass the `launch_scientist.py:363` filter, `novel_ideas = [idea for idea in ideas if idea["novel"]]`.

```bash
rm -f /tmp/ai1_rcpt
python3 - <<'PY'
import os, os.path as osp, secrets

# Poisoned ideas.json entry; "novel": True passes launch_scientist.py:363.
nonce = "canary-" + secrets.token_hex(8)
idea = {"Name": f"adv$(printf %s {nonce} >/tmp/ai1_rcpt)", "novel": True}

# launch_scientist.py:167-168
idea_name = f"20260803_120000_{idea['Name']}"
folder_name = osp.join("/tmp/runs", idea_name)
# perform_writeup.py:16-18
folder = osp.abspath(folder_name)
cwd = osp.join(folder, "latex")
writeup_file = osp.join(cwd, "template.tex")
# perform_writeup.py:80 - exact sink, unquoted
os.popen(f"chktex {writeup_file} -q -n2 -n24 -n13 -n1").read()
print("OBSERVED canary:", open("/tmp/ai1_rcpt").read() if osp.exists("/tmp/ai1_rcpt") else "<none>")
PY
```

Observed (no `chktex` on `PATH`; nonce is random per run):

```
/bin/sh: chktex: command not found
OBSERVED canary: canary-e9a4b9aed36f0670
```

## Impact / scope

Needs control of `idea['Name']` — a poisoned `ideas.json`/`seed_ideas.json` loaded under `--skip-idea-generation`, or prompt injection that steers the ideation LLM's output. The `chktex` call runs on every writeup; only a `Name` containing shell metacharacters triggers execution. Effect is command execution with the AI-Scientist process's privileges; no remote service is in scope.

## Suggested change

`subprocess.run(["chktex", writeup_file, "-q", "-n2", "-n24", "-n13", "-n1"], shell=False)` instead of `os.popen`, and reject/slug `idea['Name']` to `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+` at `launch_scientist.py:167`. The same applies to the two v2 sinks (`perform_writeup.py:684`, `perform_icbinb_writeup.py:1047`). Happy to open a PR.

```text
Built hermes-agent
error: Failed to install: typing_extensions-4.16.0-py3-none-any.whl (typing-extensions==4.16.0)
Caused by: Read-only file system (os error 30)
```

## Root cause / intent

- `nix/python.nix:154-156` deliberately creates an immutable, source-editable uv2nix environment. Source-editable does not mean dependencies are writable.
- `nix/devShell.nix:55-57` exports `VIRTUAL_ENV` to that store environment to support `uv run --active --no-sync`. Consequently `uv pip install` selects it as its write target.
- `nix/hermes-agent.nix:250-252` separately exports `HERMES_PYTHON` to that interpreter. Simply activating a different venv without addressing interpreter selection can leave the launcher/tests using the old environment.
- The development docs (`website/docs/getting-started/nix-setup.md:904-920`) say dependencies are installed into `.venv` on first entry and refer to a dependency-install stamp. That is misleading for the current Python shell.

Related intentional behavior: #77879 aligned `HERMES_PYTHON`, `python`, and `VIRTUAL_ENV` to the same environment. Preserve that invariant rather than merely unsetting one variable.

## Verification performed

Using the exact reported store environment, explicitly setting `VIRTUAL_ENV` and running `uv pip install --dry-run -e '.[acp]'` selected that store path and planned package installation. No mutation of the Nix store was attempted during investigation.

ACP is already installed in this environment. Running the actual adapter check against the live checkout succeeded:

```sh
HERMES_PYTHON_SRC_ROOT="$PWD" /nix/store/rl11cymh5x3dipdg3wdlkf2k70xy3dw8-hermes-agent-editable-env/bin/python -m acp_adapter --check
# Hermes ACP check OK
```

Thus the immediate ACP use case needs no pip install; use the Nix-provided Python/ACP entry point.

## Requested fix

Clarify and support the development workflow without weakening immutable runtime packaging:

- Correct the docs to distinguish the sealed source-editable Nix environment from a writable dependency-development venv.
- Document that bundled extras such as ACP do not require `uv pip install` in the default flake shell.
- Provide an explicit writable development-shell/venv path for contributors who need to install or change dependencies, keeping `python`, `VIRTUAL_ENV`, and `HERMES_PYTHON` aligned. Do not chmod/copy-mutate the store or silently replace the reproducible default with network installs.

Acceptance: exercise fresh and repeated `nix develop` / direnv activation; the documented mutable workflow must install an editable extra into a writable path and import it using the same interpreter the launcher/test runner uses. The sealed default should continue to run `uv run --active --no-sync` and the ACP check without package installation.

audit.title: [Bug]: Matrix: TTS audio (MEDIA delivery) silently fails — send_voice() rejects is_voice kwarg
audit.body:
### Bug Description

On Matrix, every TTS audio attachment routed through gateway MEDIA delivery (e.g. the `text_to_speech` tool result) fails to be sent. The user receives nothing — no audio, no fallback notice — and the only trace is a single WARNING in `gateway.log`:

```
WARNING gateway.platforms.base: [Matrix] Error sending media: MatrixAdapter.send_voice() got an unexpected keyword argument 'is_voice'
```


### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a Matrix gateway with a TTS provider configured (any provider; ours is a custom `piper-docker` command provider producing `.ogg`/Opus).
2. Send a message that triggers `text_to_speech` and returns a `MEDIA:` path (gateway media delivery).
3. Observe the agent replies in text, the audio is generated locally, but nothing arrives in Matrix.
4. `gateway.log` shows: `[Matrix] Error sending media: MatrixAdapter.send_voice() got an unexpected keyword argument 'is_voice'`

### Expected Behavior

The TTS audio is uploaded to Matrix as an MSC3245 voice message (Ogg/Opus) and appears as a playable voice bubble in Element.


### Actual Behavior

The audio never reaches the chat. Log output:

```
2026-09-18 19:58:59,437 INFO gateway.platforms.base: [Matrix] Delivering 1 non-image MEDIA attachment(s)
2026-09-18 19:58:59,437 WARNING gateway.platforms.base: [Matrix] Error sending media: MatrixAdapter.send_voice() got an unexpected keyword argument 'is_voice'
```

(The base-class media delivery failure notice `_notify_media_delivery_failure` did not surface either on v0.21.0; the error was silent from the user's perspective.)

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
## Affected Component

Gateway — **Matrix platform adapter** (`plugins/platforms/matrix/adapter.py`).

Note for the "Affected Component / Messaging Platform" form field: the dropdown doesn't list Matrix, so I selected the closest generic option — the affected adapter is the Matrix one, named here and throughout this issue (the bug is in `plugins/platforms/matrix/adapter.py::send_voice()`, triggered by the MEDIA delivery path in `gateway/platforms/base.py`).

Not uploaded publicly: the local `hermes debug share --local` report contains verbatim personal chat content, so I'm pasting only the relevant gateway.log lines above. Happy to run `hermes debug share` on request.
```

### Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu 26.04, kernel 7.0.0-31-generic)

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

0.21.3

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
- v0.21.0 (2026.8.31) — original occurrence, confirmed live
- Still present on v0.21.3 / commit `1e4952ddba` (current main as of 2026-09-18), verified in source: `git show origin/main:plugins/platforms/matrix/adapter.py`
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`gateway/platforms/base.py` (non-image MEDIA delivery loop) calls:

```python
result = await self.send_voice(chat_id=chat_id, audio_path=path, metadata=metadata, is_voice=is_voice)
```

The base-class `send_voice()` signature accepts `**kwargs`, but the Matrix adapter overrides it with a **narrower signature**:

```python
async def send_voice(
    self, chat_id: str, audio_path: str, caption: Optional[str] = None, reply_to: Optional[str] = None,
    metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> SendResult:
```

No `**kwargs` / no `is_voice` param → `TypeError: ... unexpected keyword argument 'is_voice'`, caught by the delivery loop and reduced to the WARNING above. Other adapters (e.g. Slack) keep `**kwargs`, so only Matrix is affected.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

One line in `plugins/platforms/matrix/adapter.py::send_voice()` — accept (and ignore) the extra kwarg:

```python
async def send_voice(
    self, chat_id: str, audio_path: str, caption: Optional[str] = None, reply_to: Optional[str] = None,
    metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, **kwargs) -> SendResult:
```

Verified end-to-end on a live gateway: with this change, TTS audio delivers correctly as an MSC3245 voice bubble in Element. (`is_voice` is unused by the Matrix adapter since it always sends as voice via `_send_local_file(..., is_voice=True)`, so swallowing the kwarg is correct; an explicit `is_voice: bool = False` param would document the contract just as well.)


### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

audit.title: Fresh Windows install: 31 platform/provider plugins fail to load (missing orjson/pybase64; also nonexistent `agent.re_compat`)
audit.body:
# 全新安装后 31 个平台 / Provider 插件大面积加载失败（缺 orjson / pybase64，以及不存在的 `agent.re_compat`）

## 环境信息

| 项 | 值 |
|---|---|
| Hermes Agent | **v0.21.3 (2026.9.14)** · upstream `f0fe07af` |
| 安装方式 | `install.ps1`（非交互 `-NonInteractive -SkipSetup`） |
| HERMES_HOME | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes`（Windows 默认） |
| 安装目录 | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent`（git 安装） |
| Python | 3.11.16（install.ps1 自建 venv：`hermes-agent\venv`） |
| OS | Windows 11 |
| 启动方式 | 桌面端（Electron，`apps/desktop/release/win-unpacked/Hermes.exe`） |

## 症状

首次启动后 `logs/errors.log` 累计 **86 条**插件加载失败：

```
WARNING hermes_cli.plugins: Failed to load plugin '<name>': No module named '<module>'
```

按原因分类：

| 次数 | 原因 | 是否可自行修复 |
|---|---|---|
| 41 | `No module named 'orjson'` | ✅ 装包即可 |
| 33 | `No module named 'pybase64'` | ✅ 装包即可 |
| 12 | `No module named 'agent.re_compat'` | ❌ 模块在仓库中不存在 |

## 受影响插件（去重 31 个）

**平台适配器（20 个）**：`whatsapp` `wecom` `telegram` `teams` `sms` `slack` `simplex` `raft` `photon` `ntfy` `mattermost` `matrix` `line` `irc` `homeassistant` `google_chat` **`feishu`** `email` `discord` `dingtalk`

**模型 Provider（8 个）**：`xai` `web-xai` `openrouter` `openai-codex` `self-hosted` `nous` `fal` `basic`

**Web 路由（2 个）**：`kanban API routes` `hermes-achievements API routes`（均报 `No module named 'orjson'`）

> 每个插件在日志中出现 3 次（= 3 次启动），故总数 86。

## 已解决：`orjson` / `pybase64`（74/86）

install.ps1 的默认依赖集**不包含**平台插件所需的这两个可选依赖。手动补齐：

```bash
uv pip install --python "<HERMES_HOME>/hermes-agent/venv/Scripts/python.exe" pybase64 orjson
# → orjson==3.12.0, pybase64==1.5.0
```

修复后失败数从 **86 → 18**（剩余全部为 `agent.re_compat`）。

**建议**：install.ps1 或 `hermes deps`/`hermes doctor` 应能一键补齐平台插件的可选依赖，否则全新安装的用户会默认失去 20 个平台适配器，且**只在日志里静默失败**（UI 无任何提示）。

## 未解决：`agent.re_compat`（12 次 / 18 个插件）

剩余失败全部指向同一个不存在的模块：

```
Failed to load plugin 'feishu-platform': No module named 'agent.re_compat'
Failed to load plugin 'telegram-platform': No module named 'agent.re_compat'
Failed to load plugin 'slack-platform': No module named 'agent.re_compat'
...
```

仓库内检索证据（clean clone，`f0fe07af`）：

```bash
$ grep -rl "re_compat" hermes-agent/agent hermes-agent/plugins hermes-agent/gateway
（无输出）

$ ls hermes-agent/agent | grep -iE "compat|^re_"
interrupt_compat.py          # 无 re_compat.py
```

即：**插件引用了内核不存在的模块**，且仓库中不存在该名字的定义。疑为模块改名 / 删除后的遗留引用，或该模块在特定条件下才生成。

## 期望结果

1. 平台插件加载失败时**在 UI 或启动摘要中可见**（现在只在 `errors.log` 里，用户无从察觉）；
2. `agent.re_compat` 的引用被修复或该依赖被移除；
3. 平台插件的可选依赖可由安装器 / 一条命令补齐。

## 影响范围

迁移后 **23 个平台适配器 + 8 个 Provider 插件**不可用，含 `feishu` / `dingtalk` / `wecom` / `telegram` / `slack`。微信（`weixin`）与主流程（provider 调用、MCP、技能、记忆）不受影响。

---

*报告基于本机实测日志与仓库检索；`errors.log` 原文、完整插件清单、修复前后对比可按需提供。*

audit.title: hermes dashboard /chat: multiple tabs on the same PTY-registry attach token collapse into one session, leaking model/context between tabs
audit.body:
## Summary

Opening two browser tabs against the same hermes dashboard /chat (v0.21.3) can result in both tabs sharing the same conversation and model state, even though they're intended to be independent sessions.

## Environment

- `hermes --version` → Hermes Agent v0.21.3 (2026.9.14)
- `hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0 --port <port>`, accessed via browser
- Reproduced on both a straightforward second tab and a Chrome "Duplicate tab"

## Root causes (in the order we found them)

1. **PTY attach token in localStorage (shared across tabs on the same origin)** — `web/src/pages/ChatPage.tsx` stores the PTY attach token (`hermes.pty.token.chat`) in localStorage. Since localStorage is shared across tabs on the same origin, two tabs can reuse the same attach token and collapse into one PTY/session.

2. **Chrome "Duplicate tab" clones sessionStorage, defeating fix #1** — Chrome's "Duplicate Tab" action clones the current tab's sessionStorage into the new tab (unlike a normal new-tab open, which starts with empty sessionStorage). Any sessionStorage-based attach token isolation can be defeated by duplicate-tab.

3. **Fresh spawn silently resumes via HERMES_TUI_ACTIVE_SESSION_FILE when `?resume=` is absent** — When a `/chat` tab spawns `hermes --tui` without an explicit `?resume=` query param, the dashboard doesn't tell the client which session was chosen; backend may resume via active-session file instead of minting a visible new session.

4. **Naive fix for #3 causes a regression: minted session id was never actually created** — An initial attempt generated a new session id and passed it as `HERMES_TUI_RESUME=<id>` without first creating that row in state.db, breaking spawn/resume.

5. **Minted dashboard-PTY session id is invisible to config.set (gateway `_sessions` registry), breaking per-session model switching** — Once #1–#4 correctly isolate tabs into distinct `session_id`s in state.db, model switching via the dashboard UI still failed because `config.set model` requires a live entry in the gateway in-memory `_sessions` map; dashboard-PTY mint only wrote state.db, not `_sessions`.

## Suggested fix summary for maintainers

- **ChatPage.tsx**: sessionStorage for the PTY attach token + Web Locks duplicate-detection, both seem like reasonable permanent fixes.
- **chat_ws.py / pty_session.py**: on a fresh (unknown) attach token with no `?resume=`, explicitly create-then-resume a new session rather than relying on `HERMES_TUI_ACTIVE_SESSION_FILE`.
- The dashboard's PTY-mint path should register into whatever registry `config.set` / other session-scoped gateway RPCs expect, not just state.db — otherwise every dashboard-originated session is invisible to session-scoped RPC until some other path registers it.

## Note on discovery / testing gap

This may explain why the bug wasn't caught earlier: the documented dashboard workflow emphasizes a single active chat (resume/recap), and parallel independent web tabs appear under-tested compared to Desktop/TUI multi-session usage. Running multiple independent chats in parallel from the same browser (not one tab at a time) is a real use case for multitasking; fixes above target that scenario.

Happy to share the exact patches we applied locally if useful as a starting point.

audit.title: Bug: evolution_self_monitor fails with JSON parse error due to column order mismatch in _row_to_experience
audit.body:
## Bug Description

`evolution_self_monitor` tool returns:
```json
{"success": false, "error": "Extra data: line 1 column 5 (char 4)"}
```

## Root Cause

In `evolution/learning/observer.py`, the `_row_to_experience()` method uses hardcoded column indices (`row[0]` through `row[14]`) to read from the `experiences` table.

After schema migration v2 adds 5 new columns (`actions`, `reasoning_steps`, `result`, `confidence`, `importance`) via `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN`, the columns are appended to the end of the table. This shifts the column order, causing index misalignment.

Specifically:
- Code expects `row[9]` to be `result` (JSON object)
- After migration, `row[9]` is actually `timestamp` (date string like `2026-05-15T22:12:40.080333`)
- `json.loads('2026-05-15T22:12:40.080333')` raises `JSONDecodeError: Extra data: line 1 column 5 (char 4)`

## Actual vs Expected Column Order

**Expected (v1 schema):**
`id, experience_type, task_id, timestamp, description, context, actions, reasoning_steps, outcome, result, metrics, lessons_learned, tags, confidence, importance`

**Actual after v2 migration:**
`id, experience_type, description, outcome, task_id, context, metrics, actions, reasoning_steps, timestamp, lessons_learned, tags, result, confidence, importance`

## Fix

Replace hardcoded index access with column name mapping in `_row_to_experience()`:

```python
def _row_to_experience(self, row) -> Experience:
    # Use column name mapping to be resilient to column order changes
    return Experience.from_dict({
        "id": row["id"],
        "experience_type": row["experience_type"],
        "task_id": row["task_id"],
        "timestamp": row["timestamp"],
        "description": row["description"],
        "context": json.loads(row["context"]) if row["context"] else {},
        "actions": json.loads(row["actions"]) if row["actions"] else [],
        "reasoning_steps": json.loads(row["reasoning_steps"]) if row["reasoning_steps"] else [],
        "outcome": row["outcome"],
        "result": json.loads(row["result"]) if row["result"] else None,
        "metrics": json.loads(row["metrics"]) if row["metrics"] else {},
        "lessons_learned": json.loads(row["lessons_learned"]) if row["lessons_learned"] else [],
        "tags": json.loads(row["tags"]) if row["tags"] else [],
        "confidence": row["confidence"],
        "importance": row["importance"],
    })
```

This works because `db_pool.py` already sets `conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row`, so `row["column_name"]` is available.

## Environment
- HAE version: v7.0.13
- hermes-agent: v0.13.0
- Python: 3.11
- SQLite: 3.37 (Ubuntu 22.04)

## Impact
- `evolution_self_monitor` tool always returns error
- `get_recent_experiences()` crashes on any experience record
- Affects all evolution cycle feedback recording

MEDIUM.title: SimplePool orphans already-created items when preallocation fails partway
MEDIUM.problem: Partial SimplePool preallocation failure leaks already-created resources.

audit.title: SimplePool orphans already-created items when preallocation fails partway
audit.body:
### System Info

- TensorRT-LLM: 1.3.0rc23 (built from `f20ea652`); behaviour re-checked against `main` @ `fbda11f5`
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (sm_120), driver 595.71.05
- PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, Python 3.12.13
- Ubuntu 25.10, kernel 6.17.0-41-generic
- Backend: PyTorch; single GPU, no TP/PP
- Model where observed: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 with FP8 KV cache (where model-specific)

### Who can help?

_No response_

### Reproduction

`SimplePool` builds its preallocated items from a generator. If `create_func` raises partway through,
`_items` is never assigned and every item created up to that point is orphaned — for the process-wide
CUDA stream and event pools, up to 128 stream or 1024 event handles.

The failure that triggers this is typically memory pressure, and the leak is re-incurred on every
retry under that same pressure.

### Expected behavior

A failed preallocation destroys whatever it already created, leaking nothing.

### actual behavior

_items is never assigned and every item created so far is orphaned - up to 128 stream or 1024 event handles - and the leak recurs on each retry under the same memory pressure.

### additional notes

Destroy partially-created items when preallocation fails, and make the pools demand-driven so the
preallocation path is not used for the real CUDA pools at all.

We have the patch and 12 CPU-only tests using a plain integer factory (the pool is generic, so the
tests need no GPU): **12 fail against current `main`, 12 pass with the change.**

There is a natural follow-up — RAII for the temporary CUDA stream holder — which we would submit
separately unless you would prefer both as one PR.

**Questions for maintainers**

1. Is making the CUDA pools demand-driven acceptable, or is eager preallocation load-bearing
   somewhere we have not found?

Per CONTRIBUTING.md this Issue Request precedes the patch, which is ready and applies cleanly to `main` @ `fbda11f5`.

audit.title: TemporaryCudaStream leaks its borrowed stream when setup or exit fails
audit.body:
### System Info

- TensorRT-LLM: 1.3.0rc23 (built from `f20ea652`); behaviour re-checked against `main` @ `fbda11f5`
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (sm_120), driver 595.71.05
- PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, Python 3.12.13
- Ubuntu 25.10, kernel 6.17.0-41-generic
- Backend: PyTorch; single GPU, no TP/PP
- Model where observed: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 with FP8 KV cache (where model-specific)

### Who can help?

_No response_

### Reproduction

`TemporaryCudaStream` / `ItemHolderBase` can leak a borrowed CUDA stream back-to-pool on two paths:

1. **Partial construction.** `ItemHolderBase.__init__` acquires from the pool before `self._item` is
   established, and `TemporaryCudaStream.__init__` can raise in `wait_events` after `super().__init__`
   has taken the stream — in both cases the stream is never returned.
2. **Exit.** `__exit__` records its finish event before returning the stream, so a failure in
   `record_event()` skips the return entirely.

The leak recurs on every retry under the memory pressure that typically triggers it.

### Expected behavior

A borrowed CUDA stream is returned to its pool whether setup and exit succeed or fail.

### actual behavior

A raise during construction after acquisition, or a failure in record_event() during __exit__, skips the return entirely and leaks the stream.

### additional notes

Establish `self._item = None` before acquiring, wrap the post-acquire setup so a failure closes and
returns the stream, and make `__exit__` return the stream in a `finally` so it happens whether or not
the event was recorded.

Five CPU-only tests (the pool is faked, so no GPU is needed): they fail against the exception-safety
baseline and pass with the change.

This stacks on the SimplePool exception-safety fix, which we are raising separately. Happy to submit
them as one two-commit PR if you prefer.

Per CONTRIBUTING.md this Issue Request precedes the patch, which is ready and applies cleanly to `main` @ `fbda11f5`.

audit.title: [Bug] Attention-DP fill-gate fail-fast can skip the model-parallel status gather on a post-fill rank
audit.body:
## Description

`PyExecutor._sync_gen_only_benchmark_has_insufficient_kv()` gates the model-parallel
status gather on **rank-local dynamic state**:

```python
if (self.benchmark_req_queues_size <= 0 or self.is_warmup
        or not self._benchmark_fill_phase_active):
    return False
```

`_benchmark_fill_phase_active` is seeded from the static benchmark-disagg config but is
cleared per rank when the *global* fill gate opens (`_check_benchmark_disagg_gate`,
`py_executor.py:3995`). A rank that observes the flag clear returns before
`_allgather_model_parallel_status()`, while a peer that is still filling enters the
gather. The two ranks then run different collectives on the same communicator: the fill
gate gathers a pickled object (`MPIDist.tp_allgather`) while `_can_queue()` gathers a raw
`MPI.INT64_T` (`tp_allgather_int64`). MPI matches them by order and datatype rather than
failing, so the payloads are silently mismatched — the same failure class already
documented from a live run at `py_executor.py:4676-4679`.

This is the only site in the tree that gates a collective on rank-local state before
entering it. Its sibling `_is_benchmark_disagg_fill_complete()` states the required
discipline explicitly (`py_executor.py:3903-3905`):

> Keep going to the shared allgather even when this rank is not done so
> model-parallel ranks cannot diverge in collective order.

## Steps to reproduce

Two real MPI ranks, with the production `PyExecutor` method bound to a stub whose `dist`
is a real `MPIDist`. Rank 0 keeps `_benchmark_fill_phase_active = True`; rank 1 clears it.

```python
stub._sync_gen_only_benchmark_has_insufficient_kv([], False)
```

```
mpirun -n 2 --oversubscribe python native_vote_probe.py
```

| rank | unpatched (`f9e3e06ee7`) |
| --- | --- |
| rank 0 (`fill_active=true`) | never returns — blocked inside `MPI_Allgather` |
| rank 1 (`fill_active=false`) | returns `False` in 0.000 s, never entered the gather |
| `mpirun` | killed by a 90 s outer timeout, `rc=124` |

With the flag voted instead of read, both ranks return and agree (`mpirun rc=0`;
rank 1 spends 1.577 s waiting at the gather, i.e. it actually participates).

## Suggested fix direction

Keep only the rank-uniform `benchmark_req_queues_size` / `is_warmup` short-circuit,
carry `_benchmark_fill_phase_active` in the status tuple, and take the fail-fast decision
from the gathered result. Normal serving (`TLLM_BENCHMARK_REQ_QUEUES_SIZE` unset) still
returns before any collective, so no steady-state synchronisation is added.

## Notes

Related to #17095: this is the fill-gate allgather reported there as the first wait
point. Whether it is the whole original deadlock is not established — on this hardware
(8x L20, sm_89) the disaggregated gen-only run stalls before the GEN fill gate is ever
reached, so the original `HangDetector` -> `MPI_Abort` signature was not reproduced.

HIGH.title: Fully-masked softmax rows exponentiate to 1 in the FMHA no-loop kernel
HIGH.problem: Fully masked attention rows can exponentiate to one in the no-loop FMHA kernel.

audit.title: Fully-masked softmax rows exponentiate to 1 in the FMHA no-loop kernel
audit.body:
### System Info

- TensorRT-LLM: 1.3.0rc23 (built from `f20ea652`); behaviour re-checked against `main` @ `fbda11f5`
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (sm_120), driver 595.71.05
- PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, Python 3.12.13
- Ubuntu 25.10, kernel 6.17.0-41-generic
- Backend: PyTorch; single GPU, no TP/PP
- Model where observed: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 with FP8 KV cache (where model-specific)

### Who can help?

_No response_

### Reproduction

In `cpp/kernels/fmha_v2/src/fused_multihead_flash_attention_kernel_noloop.h`, `CHECK_NEG_INF` is
enabled only for bidirectional sliding-window, sliding-window, and custom masks. When it is compiled
out, a row whose running maximum is still `-FLT_MAX` — every score in the row masked — evaluates
`expf(-FLT_MAX - (-FLT_MAX))`, which is `expf(0) == 1`. Each masked score therefore contributes
weight 1 instead of 0.

The requirement belongs to the softmax input state, not to a mask type: any instantiation that can
present an entirely masked row is affected, including ordinary causal and padding masks.

### Expected behavior

A fully-masked softmax row contributes zero weight to the attention output.

### actual behavior

The row's running max is still -FLT_MAX, so every masked element evaluates expf(0) == 1 and the row attends masked positions with weight 1. Silent: no error, no NaN. Presents as sequence-length-banded output corruption.

### additional notes

We can demonstrate the arithmetic directly by inspection of `apply_exp_with_mask`. We do **not** have
an isolated regression test attributing our production symptom to this line alone: the fix was
deployed alongside an unrelated kernel-enumeration change, and the evidence is a multi-day production
soak rather than a controlled A/B.

A maintainer with the fmha_v2 test harness can construct the direct case far more cheaply than we
can: any causal-mask configuration whose final Q tile is partial should show masked positions
receiving weight 1 before the change and 0 after.

**Questions for maintainers**

1. Is enabling the guard unconditionally the fix you would want, or would you prefer it gated on the
   configurations that can actually produce a fully-masked row?
2. Is there a known-good harness in `cpp/kernels/fmha_v2` you would want a regression test added to?
3. Has the performance impact of the guard on previously-unguarded instantiations been characterised
   anywhere? We have not measured it.

audit.title: [Performance]: GLM-5.3-Flash on H100: auto-selected FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90 is 36-70% slower than FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE
audit.body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>vllm collect-env (abridged)</summary>

```
OS                           : Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (x86_64)
PyTorch version              : 2.13.0+cu130
CUDA runtime version         : 13.0.88
GPU                          : 8x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (single node, TP=8)
Nvidia driver version        : 595.71.05
vLLM Version                 : 0.28.1rc1.dev580+g385dce36b (git sha: 385dce36b)
Docker image                 : vllm/vllm-openai:glm53-flash @ sha256:819ec9c063412e5730d1b0e82046ba540d1bf991f3c4f661a849aae8a0c52374
[pip3] flashinfer-python==0.6.18
[pip3] torch==2.13.0+cu130
[pip3] triton==3.7.1
```
</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Summary:** For `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` on H100 the auto-selected sparse-MLA attention backend is `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` (log: `Using FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90 attention backend out of potential backends: ['FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90', 'FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE']`). It is **~36% slower at concurrency 1 and ~70% slower at concurrency 8** than the other candidate, `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE`, measured with `vllm bench serve` on the same server flags. MTP draft acceptance is identical across the two, so the gap is per-step attention cost, not speculative-decoding behaviour. Forcing `--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` recovers it.

**How we found it:** we had been serving from an image built on 2026-08-26 from the `glm-release` branch (base `487ecf187`, FlashInfer 0.6.17). That build logs `Using FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE attention backend out of potential backends: ['FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE', 'FLASHMLA_SPARSE']`. After moving to the current `vllm/vllm-openai:glm53-flash` (nightly `385dce36b`, FlashInfer 0.6.18) with identical flags, the backend line changed to `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` and single-stream throughput dropped by roughly a third. The preference appears to come from #53906 (`031c899d` "[Model] Use FlashInfer for GLM-5.3-Flash NoPE MLA", `e34f7f71` "[Kernel] Use FlashInfer rc10 for NoPE MLA") and is gated on the FlashInfer version, so the 0.6.17 -> 0.6.18 bump flipped the kernel without any flag change.

**Server launch (both runs identical except the one flag):**

```bash
docker run --gpus all --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 \
  -v /path/to/hf-cache:/root/.cache/huggingface \
  -e VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 \
  vllm/vllm-openai:glm53-flash \
  zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --served-model-name zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}' \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 512
  # "FA3" rows add:  --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE
```

**Benchmark (run inside the same container):**

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --base-url http://localhost:8000 \
  --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --served-model-name zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --dataset-name sonnet --dataset-path /vllm-workspace/benchmarks/sonnet.txt \
  --sonnet-input-len 300 --sonnet-output-len 256 --sonnet-prefix-len 100 \
  --num-prompts 20 --num-warmups 2 --max-concurrency {1,8} --ignore-eos --disable-shuffle --temperature 0 --seed 0
# "random" rows: --dataset-name random --random-input-len 300 --random-output-len 256
```

| dataset | max-concurrency | backend | output tok/s | mean TPOT | mean ITL | median E2E (256 tok) | MTP accept len / rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sonnet | 1 | `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` (forced) | **368.8** | 2.28 ms | 10.9 ms | 698 ms | 4.89 / 77.8% |
| sonnet | 1 | `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` (default) | 237.0 | 3.83 ms | 18.3 ms | 1064 ms | 4.89 / 77.7% |
| sonnet | 8 | `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` (forced) | **754.1** | 5.00 ms | 23.9 ms | 1914 ms | 4.90 / 77.9% |
| sonnet | 8 | `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` (default) | 229.8 | 17.4 ms | 82.9 ms | 5470 ms | 4.87 / 77.3% |
| random | 1 | `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` (forced) | **249.3** | 3.59 ms | 10.9 ms | 1006 ms | 3.08 / 41.7% |
| random | 1 | `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` (default) | 162.9 | 5.78 ms | 17.0 ms | 1570 ms | 2.97 / 39.5% |

(sonnet is a best case for MTP on this model, random a worst case; the ratio between backends is the same in both.) Same picture with `--enable-expert-parallel` (recipe TEP strategy) and with the Hopper recipe override `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune`.

**Expected:** the auto-selected backend should not be materially slower than an available alternative on the same hardware; or the recipe should document `--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` for Hopper.

**Related:** forcing `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` on this nightly floods the log with `Error: Failed to initialize the TMA descriptor 1` from zero-extent descriptors (outputs correct; 0 such messages with the default backend). Filed separately: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56563.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

nodes.body:
Root-caused this statically on H20 (sm_90) — the full selection chain reproduces both log behaviors in the report; sharing it since a fix decision needs the mechanism.

**Why the backend flips between your two builds.** The backend choice happens CPU-side in `platforms/cuda.py`, and for GLM-5.3-Flash it lands on the Hopper `else` branch of `_get_backend_priorities` (`use_mla=True`, major==9):

```python
sparse_tail = [FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE, FLASHMLA_SPARSE]
if head_size == 512:
    sparse_tail.insert(0, FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90)   # ← unconditional top priority
```

`head_size = kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim = 512 + 0 = 512` (NoPE config), so `insert(0, ...)` puts `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` **ahead of** `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE`. The first four non-sparse candidates are all rejected (model requires sparse), so the winner is decided inside `sparse_tail`.

The version flip is the feature gate: `flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py::supports_combination` calls `has_flashinfer_sm90_nope_mla()`, which checks for the `ckv_scale_arr` kwarg on `BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper.run` — introduced in FlashInfer **0.6.18**.

- 0.6.17 (your glm-release build): gate rejects → falls through to **FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE** (fast path)
- 0.6.18 (your nightly): gate passes, `kv_lora_rank == 512` ✓ and `qk_rope_head_dim in (0, 64)` ✓ → **FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90** (36–70% slower per your numbers)

Both of your logs are exactly what this chain predicts. The `insert(0, ...)` was introduced by `98ed0856f3` / #53906 — the same change the issue points at. The intent (FP8 KV in-kernel dequant, half HBM traffic on Hopper) is reasonable, but there is no benchmark backing the priority **inversion** on sm_90, and your data (MTP accept length identical → the gap is purely the per-step attention kernel) says the inversion is backwards at least for this model.

**Possible fix directions:**

1. Demote the Hopper FlashInfer sparse backend from `insert(0, ...)` to `append` (behind FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE);
2. Keep the priority but document `--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` for sm_90 recipes;
3. Make it batch-size adaptive — your numbers show the gap widens at low concurrency (36% @ 1 vs 70% @ 8).

Also worth handling together with #56563 (the TMA descriptor zero-extent error spam when forcing FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE — output correct but log-spammy), since option 1 would route more users onto that backend by default.

**Honest scope note:** I could not run the throughput A/B on my side — GLM-5.3-Flash's only published weights are FP8 at 328 GB, which doesn't fit 2×96 GB. The chain above is verified against upstream main `75c71390d` source and the model's config.json; the selection logic is fully CPU-side, so the analysis holds independently of memory. If someone with H100s runs the A/B, the numbers in this issue already cover it.

audit.title: [Bug] The missing DSL-compiler WASM hides its prerequisite instead of naming it
audit.body: ### Proposed Workgroup Developer Experience & Ecosystem ### Describe the bug When the DSL-compiler WASM is not built, the failure hides the prerequisite instead of naming it. The DevEx charter (#2970) commits to improving "time to the first successful result **without hiding prerequisites** or cached state". Three signals mislead at once: **1. The asset request looks successful.** `/signal-compiler.wasm` is answered by the Vite SPA fallback with **HTTP 200 and `index.html`**, not a 404, so nothing looks missing. `lib/wasm.ts` then hands that HTML to `WebAssembly.compileStreaming`, which reports the wrong problem: ``` Incorrect response MIME type. Expected 'application/wasm'. ``` **2. The badge names the subsystem, not the problem.** `stores/dslStore.ts:52-62` captures the message (`set({ wasmError: msg })`) but only logs it to the console, and `pages/builderPageToolbar.tsx:118-121` renders the literal string with no `title` and no `aria-label`: ```tsx {wasmError ? ( WASM Error ``` **3. The workspace is silently empty.** Models, Signals and Routes all read 0 and every panel is blank — which reads as "the app is broken" or "my config is empty". Nothing states that the WASM is a separate build artifact. `dashboard/README.md` documents `make dashboard-dev-frontend` (which builds it) but never says `npm run dev` alone does not. ### To Reproduce ```bash mv dashboard/frontend/public/signal-compiler.wasm /tmp/ # hard-reload http://localhost:3001/builder ``` Red "WASM Error" badge, no tooltip, all counts 0, request returned 200, and the only accurate message in the console. Building it (`make dashboard-build-wasm`) and reloading fixes it at once. This is the state reached by running `npm run dev` — the natural frontend command, and the only option on hosts without `make` — instead of the documented `make dashboard-dev-frontend` wrapper. ### Expected behavior Name the prerequisite where it fails. Minimum — surface the message already captured, following the pattern the same file uses for its other controls (8 uses of `title`, e.g. lines 137, 156, 174, 195): ```tsx ``` Better — have `lib/wasm.ts` distinguish "artifact missing" from "wrong content type" before compiling, and say `Run make dashboard-build-wasm` in the thrown message. ### Impact A contributor following the natural frontend workflow reaches an empty Config Builder with a two-word badge, a 200 response, and a MIME error pointing away from the cause. Recovering requires knowing the WASM is a separate build artifact — a prerequisite the current failure hides. ### Additional context The badge has been in this shape since `5a7ab10008` (2026-03-08); no issue or open PR covers it. The neighbouring controls already establish `title` as the pattern for explaining state.

audit.title: Greedy decoding is not reproducible across server restarts when FlashInfer autotune is enabled (DFLASH speculative decoding)
audit.body:
# Greedy decoding is not reproducible across server restarts when FlashInfer autotune is enabled (DFLASH speculative decoding) ## Summary With `temperature=0, top_k=1` (greedy), a DFLASH speculative-decoding server produces **different output text across restarts of the same server process** for the same prompt, even though sampling is deterministic. Starting the server with `--disable-flashinfer-autotune` removes the effect: two independent restarts then produce byte-identical output (8/8 test prompts). A non-speculative (plain autoregressive) server on the same model was reproducible across restarts with autotune either way. We hit this while building a reproducible benchmark for a talk, where identical greedy output across restarts is required. ## Environment - SGLang: `0.0.0.dev1+g5f55db35e` - PyTorch: `2.13.0+cu130` - CUDA (torch): `13.0` - FlashInfer: `0.6.17` - Container image: `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13-qwen38-27b-dflash2` (public; `lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:616a3e97f45191af975896cfa644279096cb31bd408a071c2e99ca7209c3cafe`) - GPU: NVIDIA GB10 (Grace Blackwell), `sm121`, 121 GB unified memory - Base model: `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (NVFP4 weights, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`) - Draft model: `incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` (canonical; we ran the mirror `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` at revision `50307d4c4cde6860d4eee73e2547cd786fe8e8a4`), `--speculative-algorithm DFLASH`, `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 8` ## Reproduction Greedy, identical requests. `enable_thinking=false` keeps output bounded (this base model is a reasoning model); the effect does not depend on it. Warm up once after each start, because the first full generation after a start is transient (a separate effect) — the warmup isolates the restart effect. A self-contained script (no external repo, one built-in prompt) is below. It starts the server, warms up, generates, hashes, restarts, repeats, and compares.
repro_autotune.py — starts server, restarts, compares greedy output ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 # Reproduce: greedy output differs across sglang restarts with FlashInfer autotune ON. # python3 repro_autotune.py # autotune ON -> expect DIFFERENT # python3 repro_autotune.py --autotune-off # autotune OFF -> expect IDENTICAL # # Defaults use our exact setup (needs a Blackwell GPU for the NVFP4 weights). To test # the hypothesis on commodity hardware (e.g. H100/A100) with a standard model and a # different speculative algorithm, override via env, for example: # MODEL=meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct SPEC_ALGO=EAGLE \ # DRAFT=yuhuili/EAGLE-LLaMA3.1-Instruct-8B NUM_DRAFT=8 python3 repro_autotune.py # For algorithms that need no separate draft model, leave DRAFT empty. import subprocess, sys, time, json, hashlib, urllib.request, os MODEL = os.environ.get("MODEL", "RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4") SPEC_ALGO = os.environ.get("SPEC_ALGO", "DFLASH") DRAFT = os.environ.get("DRAFT", "incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2") # we verified with mirror z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 @ 50307d4c DRAFT_REV = os.environ.get("DRAFT_REV", "") # optional pin NUM_DRAFT = os.environ.get("NUM_DRAFT", "8") PORT = int(os.environ.get("PORT", "30000")) AUTOTUNE_OFF = "--autotune-off" in sys.argv URL = f"http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}" PROMPT = ("Write a Python function word_count(text) that returns a dictionary mapping each " "word to its count, case-insensitive and ignoring punctuation. Include a docstring " "and type hints. Code only.") def start(): cmd = ["python3","-m","sglang.launch_server", "--model-path",MODEL,"--served-model-name","repro","--trust-remote-code", "--speculative-algorithm",SPEC_ALGO, "--speculative-num-draft-tokens",NUM_DRAFT, "--host","127.0.0.1","--port",str(PORT)] if DRAFT: cmd += ["--speculative-draft-model-path",DRAFT] if DRAFT_REV: cmd += ["--speculative-draft-model-revision",DRAFT_REV] if AUTOTUNE_OFF: cmd.append("--disable-flashinfer-autotune") p = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=open("/tmp/sgl_repro.log","w"), stderr=subprocess.STDOUT) for _ in range(300): try: urllib.request.urlopen(URL+"/health", timeout=3); return p except Exception: time.sleep(5) p.terminate(); sys.exit("server did not become healthy; see /tmp/sgl_repro.log") def stop(p): p.terminate() try: p.wait(timeout=60) except Exception: p.kill() time.sleep(3) def gen(): body = json.dumps({"model":"repro","messages":[{"role":"user","content":PROMPT}], "temperature":0,"top_k":1,"max_tokens":320, "chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":False}}).encode() req = urllib.request.Request(URL+"/v1/chat/completions", data=body, headers={"Content-Type":"application/json"}) j = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=300)) t = j["choices"][0]["message"]["content"] or "" return hashlib.sha256(t.encode()).hexdigest()[:16], j["usage"]["completion_tokens"] def run_once(): p = start() gen() # warmup (settle the transient first generation) h, n = gen() # record stop(p) return h, n print(f"autotune {'OFF' if AUTOTUNE_OFF else 'ON'}: two restarts, greedy (temp=0, top_k=1)") h1, n1 = run_once(); print(f" restart 1: sha256={h1} tokens={n1}") h2, n2 = run_once(); print(f" restart 2: sha256={h2} tokens={n2}") print("RESULT:", "IDENTICAL" if h1==h2 else "DIFFERENT", "-- expected DIFFERENT with autotune ON, IDENTICAL with --autotune-off") ```
Equivalent manual steps: start the server; warm up (one discarded request); record `sha256(choices[0].message.content)` and `usage.completion_tokens`; stop and restart with the identical command; warm up and record again; compare. Then repeat with `--disable-flashinfer-autotune`. The prompts used in the evidence table below:
8 evidence prompts ``` word_count : Write a Python function word_count(text) that returns a dictionary mapping each word to its count, case-insensitive and ignoring punctuation. Include a docstring and type hints. Code only. hashmap : Explain what a hash map is in exactly 3 sentences. unit-tests : List 5 benefits of unit testing, one line each. tcp : Describe the TCP three-way handshake in 4 sentences. proc-thread: What is the difference between a process and a thread? 3 sentences. cap : Summarize the CAP theorem in 3 sentences. fibonacci : Write a Python function returning the nth Fibonacci number iteratively, with a docstring. Code only. ``` `pomodoro` (the long-generation prompt) in full: ``` Create a single, self-contained HTML file for a Pomodoro focus timer. All CSS and JavaScript inline — no libraries, no CDN links, no images. Requirements: - A circular SVG countdown ring that depletes as time passes (stroke-dashoffset). - Three mode buttons: Focus (25 min), Short Break (5 min), Long Break (15 min); highlight the active one. - Big MM:SS display centered in the ring. - Start / Pause and Reset buttons. - A completed-focus-sessions counter that increments each time a Focus session reaches zero. - A short beep via the Web Audio API when the timer reaches zero (no audio files). - Modern dark UI, one accent color, centered layout, rounded corners, smooth transitions. Write compact code: no comments, concise CSS (group selectors, short values). Keep the file under 110 lines. Output ONLY the complete HTML file, starting with . Nothing before or after the code. ```
## Expected vs actual - Expected: with greedy sampling, the same prompt yields identical output across restarts. - Actual (autotune enabled): different text and, frequently, a different number of generated tokens across restarts. ## Evidence Each experiment = two independent restarts, warm, same 8 prompts, greedy. ### Experiment 1 - autotune ENABLED, `--random-seed 42` pinned on both starts Per-prompt `sha256[:12]` (restart 1 vs restart 2): | prompt | restart 1 | restart 2 | |-------------|---------------------------|---------------------------| | word_count | `a1309947d12e` (181 tok) | `5ab0a01bcffd` (184 tok) | | pomodoro | `70ba72fe717a` (1381 tok) | `ca99fa9bf5cb` (1236 tok) | | hashmap | `7b3a5251f97c` (67) | `c2c514c51143` (70) | | unit-tests | `c14dfe8832c3` (101) | `b73a3b51e0c8` (129) | | tcp | `33f1f9128026` (98) | `392a9a3af403` (82) | | proc-thread | `e5ad6a67dcdd` (97) | `c5ec14b4e046` (94) | | cap | `fdc76849eff4` (72) | `aa32a00b8bd9` (70) | | fibonacci | `d3d1812f29fe` (209) | `d3d1812f29fe` (209) | 7/8 prompts differ across the two restarts; only `fibonacci` matched. The seed is pinned to the same value on both starts, so this is not a sampling-seed effect. Example of a token-count difference: 1381 vs 1236. Token-level first divergence for `word_count` between two autotune-enabled restarts (a separate autotune-ON run pair from the seed-pinned table above; 181 vs 158 tokens): first differing token at **index 43**: ``` shared context: ... each word in the given text.\n\n The restart 1: function is case-insensitive and ignores punctuation. Words restart 2: counting is case-insensitive and ignores punctuation.\n ``` This is an early argmax flip (token 43 of ~180), not a truncation artifact. ### Experiment 2 - autotune DISABLED (`--disable-flashinfer-autotune`), two restarts All 8 prompts identical across restarts (`sha256[:12]`): ``` word_count bb92924fc6e6 pomodoro 70ba72fe717a hashmap 7b3a5251f97c unit-tests a1e0272c7edd tcp a05397b13fa6 proc-thread e5ad6a67dcdd cap 630d977d8e0f fibonacci d3d1812f29fe ``` 8/8 identical between the two autotune-disabled restarts. Note: four hashes coincide between Experiment 2 and Experiment 1 / restart 1 (`pomodoro`, `hashmap`, `proc-thread`, `fibonacci`). This is expected, not a copy error: for those prompts that particular autotune-enabled run happened to select kernels numerically equivalent to the default (autotune-off) path; for the other four it did not. The autotune-off hashes are the stable reference; autotune-enabled runs coincide with them only sometimes. ### Control - non-speculative baseline, autotune ENABLED, two restarts Same base model and flags, without the `--speculative-*` block. `sha256[:12]`, restart 1 vs restart 2: | prompt | restart 1 | restart 2 | |-------------|------------------------|------------------------| | word_count | `eaaaafd3bc77` (161) | `eaaaafd3bc77` (161) | | pomodoro | `4a675495c5a2` (1289) | `4a675495c5a2` (1289) | | hashmap | `7b3a5251f97c` (67) | `7b3a5251f97c` (67) | | unit-tests | `bf81f7e6d66d` (123) | `bf81f7e6d66d` (123) | | tcp | `825395560462` (96) | `825395560462` (96) | | proc-thread | `75a8cd2c22a9` (94) | `75a8cd2c22a9` (94) | | cap | `bd35ac80b11e` (72) | `bd35ac80b11e` (72) | | fibonacci | `d3d1812f29fe` (209) | `d3d1812f29fe` (209) | 8/8 identical. With autotune enabled, the plain autoregressive path is reproducible across restarts; only the DFLASH speculative path is not, in our tests. Hypothesis for why only the speculative path is affected (not confirmed in source): the DFLASH path adds tensor shapes that plain decoding does not (the draft model plus the block-verify geometry), so autotune has more kernel decisions to make and more opportunity to select differently across runs. We have not verified this against the code. If that hypothesis holds, the root cause is the number of distinct tensor shapes the speculative path introduces, not DFLASH or NVFP4 specifically. In that case the effect should reproduce with **any speculative algorithm (e.g. EAGLE, MTP) and a standard model on any GPU** — it would not need Blackwell/NVFP4 or the DFlash2 draft (which exists only for this one model, so the exact setup above cannot be run on H100/A100). We could not test this ourselves (we have no other hardware or setup). For anyone with a commodity GPU this is likely the cheapest verification: run the script above with `MODEL` / `SPEC_ALGO` / `DRAFT` set to a standard EAGLE- or MTP-capable configuration. This is a suggestion, not a claim — we have not confirmed it reproduces outside our setup. ## Diagnosis (what we ruled out) - `--random-seed`: excluded. At `temperature=0, top_k=1` there is no sampling for the seed to affect; verified empirically (Experiment 1 pins `--random-seed 42` on both restarts and still diverges 7/8). - `--kv-cache-dtype`: the effect reproduces with both `fp8_e4m3` and `auto` (bf16), so KV cache dtype is not the cause. - Speculative block length (`--speculative-num-draft-tokens`): varying it changes which prompts diverge but does not remove the divergence. - `--disable-flashinfer-autotune`: makes the output identical across restarts (8/8), and the non-speculative baseline is reproducible regardless. Observation (hypothesis, not confirmed in source): FlashInfer autotune appears to select kernels per process start via micro-benchmark timing, and its autotune cache directory (`/root/.cache/sglang/flashinfer/autotune//sm121/...`) is not persisted across container restarts, so each start re-runs autotune and can pick different kernels, giving slightly different numerics that flip token choices under greedy. We have not verified the kernel-selection mechanism in the SGLang/FlashInfer source; this is inferred from the observed behavior and the effect of the flag. ## Performance impact of the workaround Decode throughput on the speculative server, autotune enabled vs disabled, greedy, warm (median of 5): - Short code prompt (~180 tok): 60.4 -> 57.9 tok/s (about -4%) - Longer HTML prompt (~1.3k tok): 45.1 -> 45.6 tok/s (no measurable change) ## Question for maintainers We are not attached to a specific fix and do not know the internal constraints. Is any of these feasible / preferable: - persisting the FlashInfer autotune cache across process restarts (so kernel selection is stable), or - a flag to force deterministic kernel selection while keeping autotune, or - documenting that FlashInfer autotune breaks cross-restart reproducibility under greedy, so users who need reproducible outputs know to disable it? This was observed only on GB10 / `sm121`, which is uncommon hardware. Our exact base+draft models cannot run on H100/A100 (NVFP4/Blackwell, and the DFlash2 draft exists only for this model), so a check there would use the standard-model + EAGLE/MTP path described in the Control section. A repro (or non-repro) on commodity hardware would help scope whether this is hardware- or setup-specific. Happy to run additional diagnostics on this hardware.
