audit.title: buzz-acp: idle-pool teardown race silently swallows a concurrently arriving message (no log trace beyond routine steer ack)
audit.body:
## Summary

`buzz-acp`'s idle-pool reaper (`idle_pool_sleep_due`, `crates/buzz-acp/src/lib.rs:2164-2179`, invoked from the reaper-tick `select!` arm at `lib.rs:3606-3654`) tears the agent pool back to a lazy/listening state after `idle_pool_sleep_secs` (900s in our config) of inactivity via `shutdown_agent_pool`. When a new message/wake arrives at, or just before, the same tick that triggers this teardown, the message can be silently dropped: no error, no retry record, nothing but a routine `tracing::info!` line —

```
crates/buzz-acp/src/lib.rs:3914-3922
tracing::info!(
    channel = %channel_id,
    event_id = %event_id,
    ?ack,
    release_withheld,
    drop_withheld,
    signal_fallback,
    "non-cancelling steer ack received"
);
```

— which reads as routine steer bookkeeping, not as a dropped-message signal.

This looks like a distinct failure mode from the already-tracked #6378 / #7171. Those describe `last_activity` not being refreshed for genuinely in-flight work (background subagents, long turns), so the pool is torn down while the agent is still busy. Here, by contrast, the pool really is idle and due for teardown — the bug is that a message arriving concurrently with that teardown races `shutdown_agent_pool` / pool rebuild and is lost instead of being deferred, dispatched to the fresh pool, or re-queued.

## Scope

Affects every buzz-acp managed agent, independent of `subscribe` mode (Mentions vs Config). Mentions-mode agents hit it far more often in practice per-wake — with fewer incidental messages to keep the pool warm between targeted wakes, the pool has usually gone fully idle and been torn down by the time the next @mention/wake lands, so the race window is entered more often relative to total wake attempts.

## Evidence

The `"non-cancelling steer ack received"` log line is the direct fingerprint of a steer racing pool teardown/rebuild. Counts observed in our deployment's agent logs:

- `harness-dev-orch`: 69 occurrences (highest raw count, but least visible impact — many subscribed channels mean other traffic quickly re-wakes the pool, masking the drop)
- `stock_orch`: 8 occurrences
- `stock-news`: 5 occurrences

## Real-world impact

`stock-news`'s pre-market briefing pipeline depends on a cron-triggered T-30 wake message. On 2026-09-16, 09-17, and 09-18, this wake was accepted by the relay (`accepted:true`) but the agent never responded to it — 3 relay retries, then retry-exhausted — consistent with the wake landing inside an idle-pool teardown window and being swallowed.

## Suggested repro / investigation

Dispatch a message exactly at/after `idle_pool_sleep_bound` elapses (900s default) while `pool_ready` is true and the `idle_pool_sleep_due` gates (`work_queued`, `prompt_tasks_in_flight`, `wake_or_respawn_in_flight`) are all clear, and trace what happens to that message through `shutdown_agent_pool` and pool rebuild (`lib.rs:3635-3653`). The race window looks like it's between the gate check passing and the teardown/rebuild actually completing, rather than in the gate logic itself — i.e. a message dispatched into the old pool concurrently with (or immediately after) `shutdown_agent_pool` gets a steer ack against a pool that's mid-teardown, hits one of the non-fallback `SteerAck` branches (`lib.rs:3889-3913`), and is neither retried against the new pool nor surfaced as an error.

## Related issues

- #6378 — idle pool teardown kills an in-flight session, losing a queued background-task wakeup. Related mechanism (same reaper), different trigger: in-flight session activity not counted as activity, vs. a *new* message racing the teardown of an *already-idle* pool.
- #7171 — idle-pool reaper tears down right after a long turn completes. Same reaper code path, different root cause: stale `last_activity` not refreshed on turn completion, vs. a delivery race during an already-correctly-triggered teardown.

Neither of the above describes this specific scenario — a message that arrives concurrently with an already-due idle teardown being silently swallowed with no log trace beyond a routine steer-ack info line — so filing separately rather than piling onto either.

audit.title: Mobile startup issues a burst of ~106 relay /query requests, 27 of them empty
audit.body:
Self-hosted relay, Buzz Desktop 0.5.23, mobile client. Source pinned at `c507a4d488ca27796e78d876b9c24ee38442cc1b`.

## Symptom

Opening the mobile app issues a burst of relay `/query` HTTP requests. Over a 3-minute window, one client IP produced **106 `/query`**, of which **27 had `Content-Length: 2`** (an empty filter):

```
106 x /query   (7-25 ms each, 200)
  6 x /events  (13-16 ms each, 200)
Content-Length distribution:
  27 x 2        <- empty
  18 x 5830
  14 x 427
  10 x 295
  10 x 2461
   8 x 155
```

The relay is not the bottleneck: every request returns in 7-25 ms and the relay sits at 0.5% CPU. The cost is the number of round-trips on a mobile connection.

## Expected

A single batched sync on open, then incremental updates over the existing WebSocket subscription.

## Where to look

- `mobile/lib/shared/relay/relay_session.dart` — `queryRelay()` (the `/query` bridge)
- Callers: `mobile/lib/shared/community/community_membership_provider.dart`, `mobile/lib/features/channels/channel_management_provider.dart`, `mobile/lib/features/invites/invite_create_provider.dart`

## Reproduction

Point the relay's Caddy at `log { output stdout format json level INFO }`, open the mobile app, and count `uri":"/query"` in the access log.

audit.title: tests implmentation affects pass@1 in polyglot-benchmark
audit.body:
### Issue

In the Aider Python track’s ‘grep’ exercise, I’ve found an issue relating to the test implementation of the built-in open() function. The test suite employs a mock for open():

```Python

def open_mock(fname, *args, **kwargs):
    try:
        return io.StringIO(FILE_TEXT[fname])
    except KeyError:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "Expected one of {0!r}: got {1!r}".format(list(FILE_TEXT.keys()), fname)
        )
```
This specific mock implies that the solver’s code is compelled to directly attempt to open() a file (and handle the resulting RuntimeError from the mock, or FileNotFoundError in a real scenario) rather than first checking for file existence using os.path.exists().

However, the problem specification for the exercise does not explicitly describe this constraint. From the perspective of standard Python programming practices and a literal interpretation of the problem instructions, using os.path.exists() to verify a file’s presence before attempting to open it is a perfectly reasonable and common approach.

When evaluating LLMs/agents using the Aider benchmark, this mismatch between the test’s implicit requirement and the problem’s lack of explicit guidance leads to a failure in a one-shot attempt for this specific case, as some models default to the more intuitive os.path.exists() strategy, which then fails the mock-based test.

Proposed Solutions
To address this ambiguity and improve the fairness of the benchmark, I propose the following solutions:

Direct File Provision: Similar to the JavaScript track, consider providing actual .txt files in the testing environment rather than fully mocking the open() function with io.StringIO.
Comprehensive File Operation Mocking: Implement a more extensive mock for file system operations that also covers functions like os.path.exists(), ensuring it responds predictably to simulate file existence or non-existence.

nodes.title: fix(javascript): replace removed toThrowError matcher with toThrow
nodes.body:
## Problem

Two JavaScript exercise specs use `toThrowError(`, which Jest 30 removed (it is a
deprecated alias of `toThrow`). On an image whose `jest` resolves to 30.x the assertion
throws before it can compare anything:

```
TypeError: expect(...).toThrowError is not a function
```

Affected:

- `javascript/exercises/practice/resistor-color-trio/resistor-color-trio.spec.js` (1 occurrence)
- `javascript/exercises/practice/affine-cipher/affine-cipher.spec.js` (2 occurrences)

## Why the surrounding `xtest(` does not save them

The calls sit inside `xtest(...)` blocks, which would normally be skipped. The benchmark
does not run the specs as shipped: `benchmark/npm-test.sh` unskips them before invoking
jest,

```sh
sed -i 's/\bxtest(/test(/g' *.spec.js     # benchmark/npm-test.sh:11
```

and the Java runner does the equivalent (it strips `@Disabled(...)` in `benchmark.py`).
The removed matcher therefore executes on every benchmark run.

Measured on a reference arm that scored the exercise `[False, False]`:

```
✓ Orange and orange and black
✓ Blue and grey and brown
✓ Red and black and red
✓ Green and brown and orange
✓ Yellow and violet and yellow
✕ Invalid color
Test Suites: 1 failed, 1 total
Tests:       1 failed, 5 passed, 6 total
```

Every other assertion passes; the removed matcher is the only thing keeping the case
from scoring. Across 246 local runs on one machine (140 of them attempting this
exercise, spanning many models), `resistor-color-trio` has never passed once.

## Fix

`.toThrowError(` -> `.toThrow(` in the two specs. `toThrow` is the canonical matcher and
behaves identically on jest 29 and 30, so the change is safe on both.

One caution for anyone applying this by hand: keep the call's paren structure, i.e.
`).toThrow(...)`. Introducing an extra `)` leaves the spec at paren depth -1, Babel
refuses to parse the file, and the case then fails harder than the original bug
(`Tests: 0 total`). The diff here is balanced.

## Tests

In the benchmark container (jest 30.4.1):

- before: `expect(...).toThrowError(...)` -> `TypeError: expect(...).toThrowError is not a function`
- after: `expect(...).toThrow(...)` -> the assertion is evaluated normally

## Scope

Only these two files. No other exercise under `javascript/` uses `toThrowError`. The
image-side alternative is Aider-AI/aider#5726 (pin `jest` to 29.x); either change fixes
the failure, and the two together remove both the dead alias and the version drift.

audit.title: Go counter receives a passing grade with zero tests executed
audit.body:
## Observed behavior

I found that the Go `counter` exercise can receive a passing grade with zero tests executed. In a frozen five-agent comparison using the Harbor Aider Polyglot adapter, the three completed agents currently show `go test` output containing `[no tests to run]` and receive reward 1. I have preserved the original scores and the full task denominator.

## Source of the behavior

At the current Polyglot revision `7e0611e77b54e2dea774cdc0aa00cf9f7ed6144f`:

- The exercise instructions ask for a test suite that detects faults in the supplied counter implementations.
- [The metadata](https://github.com/Aider-AI/polyglot-benchmark/blob/7e0611e77b54e2dea774cdc0aa00cf9f7ed6144f/go/exercises/practice/counter/.meta/config.json) declares `counter.go` as the solution and `counter_test.go` as the fixed test file.
- [The fixed test file](https://github.com/Aider-AI/polyglot-benchmark/blob/7e0611e77b54e2dea774cdc0aa00cf9f7ed6144f/go/exercises/practice/counter/counter_test.go) contains a package declaration and a placeholder comment, with no test functions.
- [The current Aider verification entry point](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/benchmark/benchmark.py#L1007-L1048) restores the declared test files before running the command and treats exit code 0 as success.
- The current Harbor adapter also restores the declared tests and grades the command exit status.

One observed agent wrote a test suite during its first attempt. Verification replaced that file with the fixed placeholder. After resolving a duplicate `Counter` declaration, the final command produced:

```text
testing: warning: no tests to run
PASS
ok counter 0.027s [no tests to run]
```

This passing grade establishes successful compilation and an empty test invocation. Test-suite quality remains unmeasured for this exercise.

Could you clarify the intended status of Go `counter` in the 225-task benchmark and the scoring policy for this empty suite? An explicit catalog note would help downstream evaluations preserve standard scores and communicate their scope accurately.

MEDIUM.title: [Desktop] Reasoning effort resets from Medium to Low when reopening a session
MEDIUM.problem: Restoring a session changes reasoning effort from Medium to Low and may persist it.

audit.title: [Desktop] Reasoning effort resets from Medium to Low when reopening a session
audit.body:
### Cline Surface

Desktop App

### Cline Version

0.0.32

### Beta version

No

### What happened?

In Cline Desktop, a session configured with **Reasoning Effort = Medium** does not restore that setting after navigating to another session and then returning.

The selector changes to **Low**. This is not only a visual mismatch: if the user sends the next message without manually selecting Medium again, the Low configuration can be sent and persisted to the backend session.

Expected behavior: reopening an existing session should restore its reasoning/thinking configuration, including `reasoningEffort: "medium"`.

Actual behavior: the restored UI config has no `reasoningEffort`, so the chat input bar applies its default value, Low.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open Cline Desktop and start or open a session with a reasoning-capable model.
2. Set Reasoning Effort to **Medium**.
3. Send a message (optional, but confirms the setting is active).
4. Switch to a different session.
5. Switch back to the original session.
6. Observe that Reasoning Effort now shows **Low** instead of Medium.
7. Send a message and observe that Low can become the effective session configuration.

### Provider/Model

Not model-specific. The issue occurs in Desktop session hydration before the next provider request, for models that expose reasoning-effort options.

### Diagnostics

Desktop App 0.0.32. The installed `cline-app.exe` frontend is unchanged. The sidecar was locally rebuilt from the official `desktop-v0.0.32` source with Bun 1.3.13 baseline for compatibility with an older non-AVX2 CPU (the separate issue described in #14066).

### System Information

OS: Windows 10 Education, version 22H2 (build 19045)
CPU: Intel Core i7-3770S

### Suspected source path

The behavior appears consistent with the Desktop frontend code in `desktop-v0.0.32`:

- `chat-input-bar.tsx` defines Low as the default and applies it when both `thinking` and `reasoningEffort` are undefined:
  - https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/desktop-v0.0.32/apps/examples/desktop-app/webview/components/views/chat/chat-input-bar.tsx#L159-L168
  - https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/desktop-v0.0.32/apps/examples/desktop-app/webview/components/views/chat/chat-input-bar.tsx#L901-L909
- `hydrateSession()` restores environment, session ID, provider, model and workspace fields, but not `thinking` or `reasoningEffort`:
  - https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/desktop-v0.0.32/apps/examples/desktop-app/webview/hooks/use-chat-session.ts#L3186-L3214
  - https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/desktop-v0.0.32/apps/examples/desktop-app/webview/hooks/use-chat-session.ts#L3273-L3328

Suggested direction: include reasoning/thinking fields in the Desktop session attach response and hydrate them into the client config. The UI should not replace an unknown/unhydrated value with Low before session configuration has finished loading.

### Workaround

After returning to a session, manually select Medium again before sending the next message.

audit.title: Bug: `kanban` daemon fails to start — missing `dist/entry.js`, then `ReferenceError: AI is not defined`
audit.body:
### What happened?

## Issue 1: `dist/cli.js` requires a file the published package doesn't ship

`hub-daemon.log` shows:

```
node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1503
  throw err;
  ^

Error: Cannot find module '<npm-global>/node_modules/kanban/dist/entry.js'
    at Module._resolveFilename (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1500:15)
    ...
    at Module.executeUserEntryPoint [as runMain] (node:internal/modules/run_main:154:5)
    at node:internal/main/run_main_module:33:47 {
  code: 'MODULE_NOT_FOUND',
  requireStack: []
}
```

Confirmed by inspecting the installed package directly — a clean `npm uninstall -g kanban && npm install -g kanban` reproduces the same result:

```
node_modules/kanban/dist/
├── cli.js
├── cli.js.map
├── index.js
├── index.js.map
└── web-ui/
```

No `entry.js` and no `dist/hub/` directory exist anywhere in the published `dist/`, despite `dist/cli.js` (or whatever spawns the per-task daemon process) requiring `dist/entry.js` at a hardcoded absolute path built from the package root.

The real file the daemon needs to run does exist, just under the bundled dependency instead:

```
node_modules/kanban/node_modules/@clinebot/core/dist/hub/daemon/entry.js
```

### Workaround (confirmed to resolve the MODULE_NOT_FOUND)
Manually creating `dist/entry.js` in the installed package with:

```javascript
import "../node_modules/@clinebot/core/dist/hub/daemon/entry.js";
```

(kanban's `package.json` declares `"type": "module"`, so this ESM side-effect import works and passes through `process.argv` untouched.) This is not a real fix — it's a local shim that's wiped on every `npm i -g kanban`.

## Issue 2: once Issue 1 is worked around, the real daemon entry throws on load

With the shim in place, `hub-daemon.log` shows a second, unrelated failure:

```
ReferenceError: AI is not defined
    at file:///<npm-global>/node_modules/kanban/node_modules/@clinebot/core/dist/hub/daemon/entry.js:182:41132
    at ModuleJob.run (node:internal/modules/esm/module_job:439:25)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:104:5)
    at async node:internal/modules/esm/loader:633:26
    at async asyncRunEntryPointWithESMLoader (node:internal/modules/run_main:101:5)
```

This is inside a minified bundle (`@clinebot/core/dist/hub/daemon/entry.js`), so I can't identify the specific source construct that produced it, but the error is consistent and reproducible — it fires immediately on every daemon start attempt, not intermittently.

## Impact
Any board task that needs the daemon to (re)launch a session — e.g. a task in a git worktree that isn't already running — fails immediately with "Task failed to start" and produces no usable session output. Existing already-open sessions are unaffected; this only blocks (re)starting new ones. Saved transcripts on disk (`~/.cline/data/sessions/<session-id>/*.messages.json`) are unaffected by this bug — they're written independently of daemon health, so no chat history is lost, just inaccessible from a fresh task run.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `npm install -g kanban` (fresh install, no prior version).
2. Start the kanban server, create/open a task that requires spawning a new daemon session (e.g. a task in a fresh git worktree).
3. Observe "Task failed to start" in the UI with no session content.
4. Check `~/.cline/data/logs/hub-daemon.log` for the `MODULE_NOT_FOUND: dist/entry.js` stack trace.
5. (Optional, to see Issue 2) Apply the `dist/entry.js` shim above, restart the daemon, and observe the `ReferenceError: AI is not defined` trace instead.

### Expected behavior

Task sessions start normally without manual patching of the global install.

### Kanban version

0.1.70

### Environment

- Install method: `npm install -g kanban` - Node.js: v24.16.0 - OS: Windows 11 - Installed package location: global npm prefix, `node_modules/kanban`

nodes.body: CLINE-2969

Independent reproduction on 0.1.70, Windows, Node v24.15.0, agent claude. Fresh install after npm cache clean --force still reproduces. Confirmed dist/ ships only cli.js, index.js, their maps and web-ui/ - no entry.js and no dist/hub/ anywhere. The real daemon entry is present at node_modules/@clinebot/core/dist/hub/daemon/entry.js (654 KB), so the package ships the file, just not where the daemon looks for it. Every task fails immediately with state failed and pid null; hub-daemon.log shows the same MODULE_NOT_FOUND trace.

Independent reproduction on 0.1.70, Windows, Node v24.15.0. Adding detail on issue 2: in node_modules/@clinebot/core/dist/hub/daemon/entry.js the identifier AI is referenced at line 182 in the expression C(L,AI) and is never declared anywhere in the bundle - no var/let/const AI, no import ... as AI binding, no function declaration and no assignment. Two references, zero definitions. It looks like a namespace object the bundler failed to emit, so the daemon entry throws on load regardless of how it is reached, which is why the dist/entry.js shim only moves the failure one step later. Also checked published tarballs for 0.1.40, 0.1.50, 0.1.55, 0.1.60 and 0.1.66 through 0.1.70 - none ship dist/entry.js or dist/hub/daemon/entry.js, so there is no version to downgrade to.

audit.title: Perf: a single card with ~100KB prompt (pasted runtime logs) makes the whole board extremely slow to open and laggy
audit.body:
### What happened?

### Summary

A kanban workspace whose `board.json` contains only **7 cards** renders extremely slow when entering the board, and interactions stutter heavily. Investigation shows one card carries a **~100KB `prompt` field** — the full runtime log of `main.py` (80k+ characters) was progressively appended into the card. The other 6 cards combined are less than 5KB.

### Evidence

- `board.json` of workspace `strategy-condorder-engine-v1-1-4`: 7 cards; the largest card's `prompt` ≈ 100KB of raw log text; remaining 6 cards < 5KB in total.
- The big card's `updatedAt` is 14:43; it was fed with logs between 09:28–14:43 (matching the time the lag was reported as "especially bad today").
- Board meta shows **139 revisions** on this workspace vs ~76 on other workspaces; size inflation ≈ 34× (174KB vs 5KB).
- A comparable v1.1.5 workspace (same kind of strategy-engine project) has only 86KB `sessions.json` / 5.7KB `board.json` — a ~30× difference. This workspace ID is a v1.1.4-era ID mapped into a v1.1.7 directory, i.e. an inherited old workspace with accumulated session data and stale prompts left on cards.

### Suspected cause chain

1. Card holds 100KB of `prompt` text (raw runtime logs)
2. Frontend puts the whole card — including the full prompt text — into DOM / React state
3. React component-tree diff + Safari text rendering (CJK text is especially expensive to render)
4. Main thread blocked for a long time → severe lag

System context amplified the perceived lag (Parallels VM at 125% CPU / 6.5GB RAM, plus concurrent LLM batch runs), but the direct cause is the 100KB text being fully rendered.

**Bottleneck classification:** CPU (rendering) is the primary cause; memory pressure (4.2GB swap, VM holding 6.5GB) is an amplifier. Disk/network have been ruled out (localhost, plenty of disk space, clean git).

### Immediate workaround

Deleting (or moving away) that single 100KB log card from the board makes the UI immediately smooth again.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a kanban card and paste a very large text (~100KB, e.g. 80k+ characters of runtime logs) into its `prompt` field.
2. Put that card on a board with a handful of normal cards, then open this board in the kanban UI (observed in Safari; CJK-containing text makes it worse).
3. Observe: the board takes a very long time to load, and scrolling/interaction stutters. Safari Web Inspector → Timelines, recorded while entering the board, shows heavy Event Dispatch / Layout time around the big card's region.
4. A/B check: delete or move away the big card → the board becomes immediately responsive.

### Expected behavior

- The board should load quickly and stay responsive regardless of individual card field sizes.
- The card view should not render the full `prompt` text: long fields should be truncated with a "show more" affordance (Slack-style), e.g. cap rendered prompt at ~5KB.
- Ideally, extremely large payloads written into a card's `prompt` field should be capped at write time (e.g. > 5KB → store only a summary; full logs kept as a file/external reference), so runtime logs never bloat `board.json` and the DOM.

### Kanban version

v0.1.70

### Environment

macOS 14.6

audit.title: cline-agent/claude-model: Permission-approval dialog never renders in chat UI — Write/Bash/WebFetch/gh calls silently rejected despite working Claude auth
audit.body:
### What happened?

In the Cline Kanban chat UI, any Claude Code tool call requiring interactive permission approval (`Write`, `Edit`, mutating `Bash` — redirection, `tee`, `python3 -c`, `node -e` — `WebFetch`, `WebSearch`, `gh`) is rejected with `"Claude requested permissions to ... but you haven't granted it yet"` or `"This command requires approval"`. **No approval dialog/prompt ever appears anywhere in the UI** for the user to click "Allow." This makes it impossible to create/edit files, run non-read-only shell commands, or reach the network from within a session.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In Cline Kanban, open a session using the **Claude Sonnet 5** model via the Cline agent (configured in Kanban's model settings).
2. Ask the agent to create a simple file (e.g. "create hi.txt with 'hello world'").
3. The `Write` tool call is rejected with a permission error.
4. Confirm there is no approval dialog anywhere in the UI to grant it.
5. Same result for any mutating `Bash` command, `WebFetch`, `WebSearch`, and `gh` (even read-only `gh auth status`).

### Additional findings

- A project-level `.claude/settings.local.json` with an explicit matching allow-rule (e.g. `"Write(/opt/cline-kanban-board/workspace/test-cli/**)"`) is **not honored** either — the same call is still rejected even though it should auto-approve per standard Claude Code permission semantics.
- Read-only operations (`pwd`, `ls`, `cat`, `find`) work fine — only mutating/exec/network operations are affected.
- The `update-config` skill (intended to fix permission/settings issues) also requires the same blocked approval to run — no self-service escape hatch exists from inside chat.
- **This is not an authentication or model-access problem.** Claude is authenticated via environment variable, on an active Claude subscription, and using Claude directly in Cline Kanban for normal conversation works fine. The failure is isolated specifically to the tool-permission-approval flow for actions that require user consent (Write/Bash/WebFetch/etc.) — not to model connectivity, auth, or billing.

### Expected behavior

Either the approval dialog should render in the UI so the user can click Allow, or existing matching `.claude/settings.local.json` allow-rules should be honored so no prompt is needed at all.

### Kanban version

0.1.70

### Environment

- Backend: Claude Sonnet 5, via Cline agent, configured in Cline Kanban settings
- Claude auth: environment variable, active subscription — confirmed working for normal chat/model use
- Working directory reported to the agent differs from actual: `/root/.cline/worktrees/dcrsy/test-cli` (env info) vs `/opt/cline-kanban-board/workspace/test-cli` (actual `pwd`) — possibly related, possibly a red herring
- Observed: 2026-08-09

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, Node 22.23.2, npm 10.9.8, claude-code 2.1.226

nodes.body:
Interactive output has to be treated as a contract, not a side effect. Once a person is steering an agent through a Python session, wrong or partial output can lead to the next decision being confidently wrong.

I'm building MartinLoop because coding-agent work needs stronger operational truth. The system should tell you what ran, what changed, what verified, and where the evidence stopped being reliable. That sounds basic, but it is the difference between an agent that can demo and an agent you can hand real work to.

Would love to hear what output guarantee matters most to people using SWE-ReX interactively. MartinLoop is open source: https://github.com/Keesan12/martin-loop. We welcome feedback at support@martinloop.com.
